title: Combining successful junta restrictions
statement: Let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\{\pm1\}$, let $P$ be a set of coordinates, let $z$ assign a sign to each coordinate in $P$, and let $i$ be a coordinate outside $P$. Suppose each of two optional decision trees, with coordinates available outside $P\cup\{i\}$, is either absent or correctly computes the restriction of $f$ for the assignment extending $z$ by setting coordinate $i$ to the sign encoded by $0$ or $1$, respectively. Then the optional tree obtained by querying coordinate $i$ and using these two trees as its branches is either absent or correctly computes the restriction of $f$ for the assignment $z$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite set of coordinates
$z$ assigns a sign to every coordinate in $P$
Each branch tree is optional and has available coordinates outside $P\cup\{i\}$
The zero branch is absent or correctly computes the restriction for the assignment extending $z$ with the sign encoded by $0$ at $i$
The one branch is absent or correctly computes the restriction for the assignment extending $z$ with the sign encoded by $1$ at $i$
